A1.justification: Both PDFs describe QoQ-Med and DRPO. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A-F are readable and can be matched despite added material and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original training-method comparisons, MIMIC-IV prediction experiments, ECG and localization results, ablations, and clinician-annotated reasoning examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds hyperparameter sensitivity results and reported four-run means and standard deviations.

M1.justification: The multimodal architecture, ECG-JEPA integration, training stages, hierarchical DRPO scaling, elbow-based clustering, KL regularization, and default rewards remain unchanged. The new cluster-limit and reward-weight configurations are ablations of the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CLIMB imaging/ECG coverage and MIMIC-IV length-of-stay and mortality tasks. The balanced-data experiment and reasoning examples already appear in v1; the new sensitivity tests introduce no new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain SFT, PPO, ReMax, Reinforce++, RLOO, and GRPO, alongside the same external models: LLaVa-Med, Med-R1, GPT-4o, and o4-mini. MIMIC-IV comparator membership is also unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 Table 3 adds a configuration-sweep protocol covering cluster limits of 1, 3, 10, and 20 and accuracy:IoU reward weights of 0.6:0.2 versus 0.2:0.6. Existing dataset splits, preprocessing, model sizes, and evaluation metric definitions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 extends the existing component ablations with sensitivity tests for cluster limits and reward composition in Table 3. The no-clustering and default configurations repeat v1 values; the added configurations provide a limited extension. Balanced-data, modality-removal, and reasoning-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 introduces systematic uncertainty reporting for the central comparison: Table 2 states four training runs, the checklist specifies different seeds, and Appendix Table 7 reports means and standard deviations for most methods. v1 specifies a shuffle seed but no repeated-run count or comparable uncertainty estimates. PPO and the no-KL variant lack standard deviations in Table 7; the earlier run count remains unknown.

E6.justification: Table 2 substantially revises the central results. DRPO's reported overall accuracy/F1 changes from 0.686/0.286 to 0.666/0.295, and GRPO's from 0.613/0.200 to 0.609/0.193. v2 identifies these as four-run means, so these revisions do not establish a method improvement under identical aggregation. Table 3 adds sensitivity results, while MIMIC-IV results and the existing detailed appendix tables retain their values.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, DRPO objectives, scaling and regularization formulas, clustering rule, and metric formulas are unchanged. v2 introduces no new theorem, proof, or substantive formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same generalist multimodal-model, DRPO, localization, and resource-release claims, including the 43% F1 improvement claim. Revised experimental summaries do not change these headline statements.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds explanations involving formatting-reward saturation and automatic cluster selection. Section 4.2 newly interprets vision/text as contributing more than ECG and calls for better modality balance. Appendix D.1 adds environmental-impact arguments. Existing sample-efficiency and clinical-deployment limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 revises the reported 32B training hardware from four to eight H200 GPUs and adds estimated electricity consumption of 182.4 kWh and 571.2 kWh with power assumptions. The checklist adds licensing statements. Most implementation details and the model/code release link are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Johnson et al.'s 2023 MIMIC-IV reference for an already-used dataset. The related-work discussions and positioning against earlier multimodal models and RL methods otherwise retain their substance.

P1.justification: v2 introduces numbered related-work subsections, expands the ablation and fusion discussion, updates affiliation/conference text, and adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist. The existing scientific narrative and appendix organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the ablation table and a two-part uncertainty table, expands Table 2's caption, and reflows and renumbers existing displays. Figures 1-5 and the annotated reasoning illustrations retain their content and visual design.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's point estimates, the reported four-run uncertainty and targeted sensitivity tests make the empirical evidence more informative. The benefit is limited by incomplete uncertainty coverage and unreconciled summaries: Section 4.1 now claims six winning domains while Table 2's caption still says seven, and the abstract/conclusion retain 43% while Section 4.1 reports 46%. These issues prevent a substantial overall improvement.
